title: Inference kernel hinting + versioned performance profile publishing for MHA/GQA/MoE
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: define and implement a reproducible onboarding workflow that emits a versioned performance profile and optional kernel-hint artifact for each model variant (architecture-aware: MHA, GQA, MoE). This ticket covers: 1) schema for profile + kernel-hint, 2) collection harness for microbenchmarks (per-layer latency, memory use, KV shapes), 3) compilation pipeline changes to accept hints and produce tuned kernels, 4) CLI and Console surface for publishing and pinning profiles, and 5) rollout strategy and fallbacks. Motivation: many production regressions stem from generic compilation choices that underperform for specialized architectures (e.g., MoE routing, grouped-query attention). We need deterministic profiles that teams can pin to ensure stable latency/cost after upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Define JSON profile schema with keys: model_id, model_version, architecture_tag (MHA|GQA|MoE), token_len_distribution, per_layer_microbenchmarks (latency, memory, preferred_kernel), kv_cache_shapes, compile_flags_hint, created_by, created_at, fingerprint
Implement a microbenchmark harness that runs on a CI-capable GPU (NVIDIA A100 + Ampere/scale) and produces the profile JSON for a given model tarball
Add compiler API to accept compile_flags_hint and preferred_kernel suggestions without breaking existing deterministic builds
Expose 'redwood profile publish --model <id> --version <v> --artifact <path>' CLI that uploads profile to catalog and creates immutable versioned profile entry
Console: view profile diffs between model versions and a 'pin profile' button that marks runtime to prefer this profile for serving (with audit log)
Create automated test that validates fallback behavior: when a preferred kernel is unavailable, runtime falls back to compatible kernel and emits warning metric
Document onboarding doc and checklist in Confluence linked from the ticket
work_log: 2025-02-12: Kickoff with runtime, compiler, and model-onboarding PMs. Agreed to separate profile schema from compile artifact to allow telemetry-only profiles.

2025-02-15: Prototype microbenchmark harness created (bench/harness-micro) that collects per-layer timing and peak allocation. Initial results on MHA-only GPT-like model show 18% improved throughput using grouped-Q kernel vs generic matmul.

2025-02-18: Spike with MoE: routing overhead dominates for small batch sizes. Identified two knobs: router fusion and expert-batching threshold. Added these to compile_flags_hint and kernel preference list.
2025-02-20: Design review with Compiler team. Decided to treat preferred_kernel as advisory; compiler will validate compatibility and may choose alternative under strict correctness constraints.
2025-02-24: CLI prototype 'redwood profile publish' implemented in branch github.com/redwood-inference/rtd/PR-3214. Added initial upload to profile-catalog S3 prefix.
2025-02-26: Added Console wireframe for profile diffing (link in artifacts). Need frontend tickets to implement UI and audit log entries.
2025-02-28: Integration test failing intermittently on CI for MoE profile generation due to non-deterministic GPU scheduling. Investigating; potential mitigation: pin CUDA stream ordering in harness.
design_notes: Profile is intentionally advisory: runtime must validate kernels for correctness. We will version profiles and keep immutable fingerprints to detect accidental changes.
For MoE, the profile includes router statistics (avg tokens routed per expert, top-k expert distribution) to help the compiler choose expert-batching strategies.
GQA (Grouped Query Attention) profiles will include group count and per-group sequence-length distribution to pick between grouped-kernel and fallback full-attention kernel.
We will include a 'compatibility matrix' tool to declare which GPU architectures (sm75, sm80, sm86, etc.) and driver/CUDA combos the profile was validated on.
Release plan: publish profile support in runtime-1.20 as 'opt-in'. After two-weeks of customer trials, enable automatic preference for pinned profiles behind an enterprise feature flag.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Non-deterministic microbenchmarks cause flaky profiles. Mitigation: enforce deterministic seeds, fixed input tensors, and repeat-measurement median aggregation.
Risk: Preferred kernel causes correctness issues on corner-case seq lengths. Mitigation: compiler runtime validation step and conservative fallbacks with metric alerts.

Risk: Explosion of profile artifacts for many model variants. Mitigation: provide default synthesized profiles derived from architecture class and only require full-profile generation for high-traffic models.

Risk: Customers may over-pin older profiles and miss quality improvements. Mitigation: Console will surface quality/regression alerts tied to pinned profiles and provide 'suggested upgrade' workflows.
